chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: A man kills a man deliberately. He said: "Three kaffarahs are upon him: he must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons." And he said: "Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام gave a ruling similar to that."

key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave person to be emancipated
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: two consecutive months of sawm (fasting) without interruption
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدًا: intentionally; done deliberately and not by mistake
key_terms.مِسْكِينًا: a needy person who is to be fed as part of the expiation
key_terms.يُعْتِقُ: he frees; meaning manumission of a slave

ai.seo_question: What kaffarah is required for intentional killing according to Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning deliberate killing, stating that three kaffarahs are due: freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, and feeding sixty needy persons. It also notes that Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام issued the same ruling, showing continuity in the legal teaching of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
